newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia has cheapest Asia-Pac industrial land.
newsitem.headline: Australia has cheapest Asia-Pac industrial land.

text.p: The cheapest industrial land near cities in the Asia-Pacific region is in Australia, according to a survey released on Monday.
The survey, from property group Colliers Jardine, said the four cheapest cities in the region in which to buy industrial land parcels were in Australia.
Melbourne led the way with an average price of US$25 per square metre, more than 200 times cheaper than Singapore, the most expensive.
Next cheapest were Adelaide, Perth and Hobart, with Brisbane in sixth position.
"An industrialist looking for the best value block of land to buy in Asia Pacific would head 'down under' every time," Colliers Jardine said.
For rentals, Australian cities took the top five spots, led by Adelaide at $28 per square metre.
The survey was based on fully-serviced land of around 4,000 square metres 20 kms from the city centre.
Colliers Jardine said Singapore's prohibitive price of $5038 per square metre was explained by the low availability of freehold land.
The more common form of purchase in the city-state was on a 60-year leashold, where land prices were still 10 to 15 times higher than freehold land in Melbourne.
Only two of the centres surveyed by the group were in a downturning industrial market, Bombay and Tokyo.
